question: Team statistics only (owner, 2026-11-02): is our distance run per team right, per match, better than a constant?
status: registered 2026-11-02 before any number below is computed; CPU
data: the 249 shots clips of the 10 matches, frames 300-1125 (where the per-detection kit teams exist, team_passes/plan_v3.json); tracks of .cache/gpu_shots3 (metric_v3s_link, pitch metres); M7 / M9 clips opened through src/unseal.py
teams: per-detection kit teams (team_passes/kit_v3.py kit_teams, det_smooth), mapped to the truth's sides per clip as team_passes/plan.json
ours: per track, positions smoothed by a centred moving average of 1 s (13 rows at the even frames), a detection's speed = distance between its smoothed positions 12 frames before and after / 0.96 s (none at the track's ends); every 25th frame from 300, each team's distance for that second = 10 x the mean speed of its detections then (outfield players are 10; the team's clip mean when it has none that second); summed over the seconds
truth: per side, each outfield player's positions (role player) smoothed the same way (1 s centred moving average) and sampled every 25th frame from 300: path length; summed over the side's players

per match (clips pooled).distance (primary): each side's distance (20 team-matches): relative error |ours - truth| / truth; constant: the truth's mean distance per team-second over the other 9 matches x the seconds
per match (clips pooled).share: the left side's share of the two teams' distance: absolute error; constant 0.5
per match (clips pooled).descriptive: the same with the truth's team for each detection (nearest truth person within 3 m), to separate the team labels' part

decision: each of distance and share is shown better than its constant when the 95% bootstrap interval (over matches, 5,000 draws, seed 0, paired) of mean error ours - constant lies below 0; otherwise it is not reported as measured
caveat: the truth's positions are approximate (footpoint/diag) and jitter on a 1.05 x 0.68 m grid: both sides are smoothed at 1 s, so this compares path lengths at that scale, not the distance actually run
